typicalHomeAge: 2000s (new construction dominant in suburbs); 1970s–1990s in central Austin
climateNotes: Hot semi-arid (Köppen BSh). High solar exposure, 300+ sunny days per year, occasional hail events, hot summers with mild winters. Summer temps regularly exceed 100°F.
regionalNotes: Rapid population growth has increased contractor demand and labor rates above state average. Strong housing market with mix of new construction and older teardown/rebuild projects.

introParagraphs.roof-replacement: Austin's hot semi-arid climate with over 300 days of sunshine per year creates unique demands on residential roofing. Summer temperatures regularly exceeding 100°F accelerate asphalt shingle degradation, while occasional hail events common to Central Texas can cause granule loss and impact damage. As a result, roof replacement in Austin typically involves impact-resistant materials designed to withstand both thermal stress and storm events prevalent in the region.
